statement: A governance gate's `allow` decision (e.g. `invokeCapability()`'s `InvocationDecision`) is a permission to DISPATCH a capability, never itself evidence that the capability was performed. Any caller that reaches a completion/delivery status (`DELIVERED`, `AUTHORISED`, or an equivalent terminal success state) MUST first invoke the real provider and observe a real result; a technical failure of that dispatch resolves an UNRESOLVED-class status, never a silent success. Standing, reputation, or any other reward accrual tied to "the service was delivered" MUST be gated on the real provider result, never on the gate decision alone.
classification: A new occurrence of a general 'permission vs performance' confusion: a decision that something MAY happen is conflated with a record that it DID happen. The same shape as an earlier-closed defect class in this codebase where an approval record was mistaken for a completion receipt (agentAdmissionState.ts's own header documents this for Passport/delegation approvals vs receipts) — here recurring one layer up, at the capability-invocation/service-delivery boundary rather than the admission boundary.

canaries.assertion: requestFinancialService()'s Advisor/Architect branch only reaches DELIVERED after the real provider (draftFinancialStructure/runMoneyPennyChat) is actually called and returns a successful result; a gate 'allow' followed by a provider failure resolves UNRESOLVED, and Standing never accrues for that path.

occurrences.defect: The Advisor/Architect branch returned `status: 'DELIVERED'` and called `accrueStandingBestEffort()` immediately upon `invokeCapability()` returning `decision: 'allow'`, without ever calling MoneyPenny's real Architect (`draftFinancialStructure`) or Advisor (`runMoneyPennyChat`) implementation — a governance permission was reported and rewarded as a completed service interaction that never actually happened.

notes: There is already a `capability_invocation_completed` action vocabulary in `services/registry/invocationGateway.ts` (`emitCapabilityReceipt`'s 'completed' outcome) that no caller invoked before this repair — the fix completes that existing lifecycle (`emitCapabilityInvocationCompleted`, additive export) rather than inventing a parallel 'financial service completed' event, per `inv.engineering.036`/`037`.

A future generalization worth flagging (not built here): a shared helper enforcing 'no terminal success status without a completion receipt for this exact invocationId', so a future call site cannot recreate the same shortcut by construction rather than by discipline alone.
